LESSON: WRITING 6.3.1 ESSAY WRITING – EXPOSITORY COMPOSITION

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 6
Topic 6.3: Writing 6.3.1 Essay writing – expository composition

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 6.3.1 Essay writing – expository composition. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why is writing a key aspect of communication?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify features of expository texts for self-expression
2. create an expository composition creatively and coherently

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WRITING 6.3.1 ESSAY WRITING – EXPOSITORY COMPOSITION
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Writing 6.3.1 Essay writing – expository composition helps you succeed in INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: WRITING 6.3.1 ESSAY WRITING – EXPOSITORY COMPOSITION
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify features of expository texts for self-expression

What this means
In this part you learn to identify features of expository texts for self-expression. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify features of expository texts for self-expression.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 6.3.1 Essay writing – expository composition”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify features of expository texts for self-expression. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Create an expository composition creatively and coherently

What this means
In this part you learn to create an expository composition creatively and coherently. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: create an expository composition creatively and coherently.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 6.3.1 Essay writing – expository composition to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can create an expository composition creatively and coherently. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Writing 6.3.1 Essay writing – expository composition is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 6.3.1 Essay writing – expository composition”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify features of expository texts for self-expression)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 6.3.1 Essay writing – expository composition to a partner. (skill: create an expository composition creatively and coherently)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Writing 6.3.1 Essay writing – expository composition to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify features of expository texts for self-expression.
3. Practise this skill: create an expository composition creatively and coherently.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Writing 6.3.1 Essay writing – expository composition from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Writing 6.3.1 Essay writing – expository composition: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Writing 6.3.1 Essay writing – expository composition?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why is writing a key aspect of communication?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Writing 6.3.1 Essay writing – expository composition means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify features of expository texts for self-expression.
5. Be able to: create an expository composition creatively and coherently.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
